plan.question_en: Design a planar HfO2/SiO2/Cr multilayer absorber on an aluminum substrate for solar-thermal applications, maximizing wavelength-integral mean absorption (minimizing reflectance) in the visible band and maximizing wavelength-integral mean reflectance in the NIR band at normal incidence under the stated constraints.

facets.ask: Find analogous complete coating designs for spectral selective surfaces before narrower component studies.
keyword_queries: selective solar absorber multilayer coating design visible absorption near infrared reflection

facets.ask: Find design passages describing the joint spectral function of absorbing visible and reflecting NIR.
question_queries: Which multilayer coatings combine high visible absorptance and high near infrared reflectance for solar thermal applications?

facets.ask: Seek material-specific optical performance of the requested HfO2/SiO2/Cr stack on aluminum.
keyword_queries: HfO2 SiO2 Cr multilayer solar absorber aluminum substrate optical properties

facets.ask: Seek transferable layer-thickness synthesis methods for balancing absorption and reflection bands.
question_queries: How are dielectric metal multilayer spectral filters optimized for high visible absorption and low thermal emittance?

facets.ask: Investigate the specific mechanism of Cr as an absorber layer within the dielectric stack.
question_queries: What is the role of chromium layers in enhancing visible absorption in dielectric multilayer solar selective coatings?

task_sheet.user_objective: Design a planar HfO2/SiO2/Cr multilayer absorber on an aluminum substrate for solar-thermal applications, maximizing wavelength-integral mean absorption (minimizing reflectance) in the visible band and maximizing wavelength-integral mean reflectance in the NIR band at normal incidence under the stated constraints.

subgoals.original_span: 在 400-700 nm 可见波段吸收率尽可能高（反射率尽可能低）
subgoals.operational_definition: Wavelength integral of the specified optical quantity over the band, divided by band width, for equal-s/p unpolarized light at 0 degrees. Minimizing mean_reflectance is the executable proxy for maximizing absorption in this finite-film-on-absorber context.

subgoals.objective: Maximize NIR-band reflectance to suppress heat input
subgoals.original_span: 在 700-2000 nm 近红外波段反射率尽可能高以抑制热输入
subgoals.operational_definition: Wavelength integral of the specified optical quantity over the band, divided by band width, for equal-s/p unpolarized light at 0 degrees.

application_intents.intent: Spectral selective surface for visible light heating paint
application_intents.original_span: 为可见光吸热涂料的光谱选择性表面设计吸收膜

application_intents.intent: Report power transmission into the stated semi-infinite exit substrate (aluminum) as part of the system absorptance calculation (1-R)
application_intents.operational_definition: Treat the aluminum substrate as a semi-infinite absorbing exit medium; transmission into it contributes to total system absorption but is not a separate optimization objective.

goal_relationships.coupling: G1 and G2 are spectrally adjacent goals for the same coating stack; achieving high visible absorption often conflicts with maintaining high NIR reflectance due to material dispersion and interference coupling.

explicit_constraints.constraint: Coating materials: HfO2, SiO2, and Cr only
explicit_constraints.original_span: 仅使用 HfO2 和 SiO2 与金属 Cr
膜系总层数不超过 20 层

known_data.statement: Application is a spectral selective surface for visible light heating paint
known_data.original_span: 可见光吸热涂料的光谱选择性表面

unknowns_assumptions.statement: Execution assumes 0 degree incidence, equal-s/p unpolarized light, and wavelength-integral band means, as these were not explicitly specified in the original question.
The aluminum substrate is treated as a semi-infinite absorbing exit medium for the planar-surface calculation; T_into_substrate is not zero but contributes to system absorptance.
Optical constants/dispersion for HfO2, SiO2, Cr, and Al across 400-2000 nm, fabrication tolerances, and individual thickness bounds remain to be resolved.
Numerical acceptance thresholds and objective weights are unspecified; 'as high/low as possible' is not a fixed numeric threshold.

research_questions.question: Which complete selective solar absorber designs demonstrate high visible absorption and high NIR reflectance using dielectric-metal stacks?
How do HfO2/SiO2/Cr layer structures on aluminum affect spectral selectivity and thermal emittance?
What optimization methods effectively balance visible absorption and NIR reflectance in thin-film stacks with metallic layers?

candidate_mechanisms.mechanism: Interference in dielectric layers (HfO2/SiO2) can enhance absorption in the visible by trapping light in the Cr layer while maintaining high reflection in the NIR via a Bragg-like stack or impedance matching.
Metal-dielectric composite effects or cermets involving Cr may provide intrinsic broadband absorption tuned by layer thickness.
